name: Mount Belukha and Lake Akkem
full: Mount Belukha (4,506 m, the highest point of Siberia) and Lake Akkem at the foot of its northern (Akkem) face
near: Tyungur village (start of the Akkem trail, ~40 km to the lake); Kucherla settlement (start of the Kucherla trail, 4 km from Tyungur by road)
elev: Belukha — 4,506 m (East Summit; PeakVisor gives 4,509 m), West Summit — 4,440 m; Lake Akkem — 2,050 m; Akkem mountain hut — 1,980 m; Karatyurek Pass — 3,060 m
short: Three-headed Belukha is the highest point of Altai and Siberia; Lake Akkem is a glacial lake of milky turquoise colour right beneath its 3-kilometre northern face, the end point of Altai's most popular trek.
desc: Belukha (Altai: Uch-Sumer — “three-headed”, Kadyn-Bazhy — “summit of the Katun”) is the highest point of the Altai Mountains: East Summit 4,506 m, West Summit 4,440 m, with a saddle between them. The border between Russia and Kazakhstan runs over the summit. The Akkem, Katun, Gebler and Berel glaciers flow down from Belukha; the Katun begins at the Gebler. The mountain is part of Belukha Nature Park (≈131,000 ha, zones: nature reserve 11,012 ha, specially protected 37,000 ha, recreational 83,258 ha) and of the UNESCO site “Golden Mountains of Altai”. Lake Akkem lies at 2,050 m at the foot of the Akkem face: length ≈1,350 m, width ≈610 m, depth up to 14–15 m, area ≈54 ha. The water is grey-turquoise from glacial silt, with visibility up to 1 m, a temperature of no more than +4.5 °C, and no fish. 2.6 km higher up is the Upper Akkem Lake (≈2,100 m). On the northwest shore there has been an Akkem weather station since 1932, on the west shore an Emergency Ministry base with a helipad, and 1.5 km below the lake the Akkem mountain hut. Above the lake stands the Chapel of the Archangel Michael. Three main trails lead to the lake: the Akkem trail (from Tyungur, ≈40–42 km, 2 days), the Kucherla trail (via Lake Kucherla and Karatyurek Pass, 3,060 m) and the difficult Oroktoy trail. From the lake there are day trips to the Akkem Glacier (6 km), the Valley of the Seven Lakes (6 km, +600 m) and the Yarlu valley. Climbing Belukha is category 4A, only for trained mountaineers.
guide: Stand on the western shore of Akkem at dawn — the first rays tint the Akkem face pink, and the lake reflects it if there is no wind. The Altai people consider Belukha a sacred mountain where the spirit of the Katun lives, and the Old Believers sought Belovodye (the legendary land of the righteous) nearby — so don't make noise and don't climb the mountain “just because”. Make a day trip to the Valley of the Seven Lakes: 6 km up, and you're above the clouds with a view of the whole Akkem face. Check in with the border guards at the lake — keep your passport in a waterproof bag. And buy flatbreads at the weather station — it's a local tradition.
see: The Akkem (northern) face of Belukha; Lake Akkem and the Upper Akkem Lake (2.6 km higher); the Akkem Glacier (6 km from the lake); the Valley of the Seven Lakes (6 km, +600 m); the Yarlu valley (“White Stone”); the Chapel of the Archangel Michael; the Akkem weather station (since 1932); Karatyurek Pass (3,060 m) with a panorama of Belukha; along the way — Kuzuyak Pass and the “Three Birches” tract
skip: If you have 1–2 free days and aren't fit enough for 40 km of trail with 1,000 m of gain — you can only see Belukha from a helicopter or after 2 days on foot/horseback. If you aren't ready for cold nights (snow is possible even in August) and for having no mobile coverage.
diff: The trek to Lake Akkem is medium-hard: ≈40–42 km one way, ≈1,000 m of gain from “Three Birches”, 2 days. Via Karatyurek it is hard (climb ≈1,400 m, descent ≈1,100 m). Climbing Belukha is 4A and requires mountaineering training.
when: July–August (the most stable weather; up to +15…+23 °C in the valleys by day, around 0…+5 °C at the lake at night, snow possible); June and September — snow on the passes, cold; in winter down to −30 °C, the Akkem hut takes guests from January to mid-March
hours: Natural area — open 24 hours. The Akkem hut — summer season and January to mid-March (2026). The weather station works year-round.
daytime: Dawn and early morning — Belukha is most often visible without clouds; by lunchtime the summit is usually covered
how: To Tyungur: from Gorno-Altaysk ≈450–490 km (6–8 h) along the Chuysky Trakt (R256 highway) to Shebalino/Cherga, then via Ust-Kan and Ust-Koksa; from Barnaul ≈600 km, ≈13 h (via Cherga, Besh-Ozek, Ust-Kan, 2019). Bus Gorno-Altaysk — Tyungur (sole trader Maymanov) at 10:00, Tue–Sun, from 3,677 ₽; to Ust-Koksa — 10:00, 12:05, 12:10 (from 2,530 ₽, 6.5–8.5 h). From Tyungur: on foot/by horse over Kuzuyak Pass to the “Three Birches” tract (17 km, you can get a GAZ-66 lift), then 25 km up the Akkem to the lake; or via Kucherla, Lake Kucherla and Karatyurek Pass; or by helicopter (departure from the Chemal district, landing at the lake).
needcar: Yes: to Tyungur — bus/car; on the trail — your feet, horses, a GAZ-66 to “Three Birches”, a helicopter
self: Yes, the trail is well trodden and popular; independently — with group registration with the Emergency Ministry (online at forms.mchs.gov.ru), a passport and multi-day hiking experience. Climbing Belukha — only with mountaineering training/a guide.
roadtype: Paved road to Ust-Koksa with stretches of crushed stone (part of the way via Cherga/Ust-Kan is graded road); Ust-Koksa — Tyungur ≈30 km of crushed stone (2019); then a dirt road for a GAZ-66 to “Three Birches”, then only a horse-and-foot trail (rocks, roots, streams)
traveltime: Gorno-Altaysk — Tyungur 6.5–8 h; Tyungur — Lake Akkem 2 days on foot (1 day if you're fit or with a lift to “Three Birches”); via Kucherla and Karatyurek 3–4 days; helicopter ≈3 h (round trip with a landing)
stay: Tyungur: Vysotnik tourist complex (7 Zarechnaya St.; tents 500 ₽/person/night, cottages; 2GIS 4.9 from 79), Altai u Beryoz (8 Zarechnaya St.; beds 1,300 ₽/night, camping 250 ₽/person). Kucherla: Yelovaya Opushka (2,500 ₽/room, 2024). At the lake: Akkem mountain hut (1,980 m; economy 12,000 ₽/8-bed room, comfort 18,000 ₽/4-bed room, 2026), Active Life campsite (tents on platforms, banya, canteen), free tent sites by the Emergency Ministry base on the west shore, overnight stays at the weather station.
net: MTS and Beeline — in Tyungur and Kucherla; there is no mobile coverage on the trail or at the lake (you only get a signal on Karatyurek Pass). The weather station has satellite communication and charging; the Akkem hut has paid communication/Wi-Fi.
entry: Tourists do not need a separate ticket/permit for Belukha Nature Park (T—Zh, 2024). From 01.07.2026 the fee for visiting regional protected areas of the Altai Republic is 300 ₽ (the previous rate for Altai Republic residents); its applicability to Belukha Park has not been confirmed. There is no resort fee. A boat across the lake — 300 ₽ (2024).
transfer: Gorno-Altaysk — Tyungur: bus from 3,677 ₽ (2026), minibus ≈2,400 ₽ (2024); GAZ-66 Tyungur — “Three Birches” from 3,000 ₽/person or 15,000 ₽/vehicle (2026); horse 4,000 ₽/day (2026); helicopter from 770,000 ₽ per aircraft (2026)
bring: Passport (original; for foreigners — an FSB permit), compulsory health insurance policy and tick-bite insurance, a warm sleeping bag (comfort rating around 0 °C), a down jacket, hat and gloves, a waterproof shell, trekking poles, sandals for fords, gas/stove, a food supply (there are no shops on the trail), sunscreen and sunglasses, repellent, a first-aid kit, a power bank, cash (flatbreads, boat, banya)
warn: Border zone: the Katanda rural settlement (Tyungur, Kucherla) is in the border zone — for Russian citizens a passport is enough, and at the lake you must check in with the border guards; foreigners need a permit from the FSB Border Directorate (up to 30 working days), and for the 5-km strip along the border everyone needs a permit. The summit of Belukha is the border with Kazakhstan; crossing to the Kazakh side is prohibited (fines). Cold and snow even in August, sudden weather changes, fords of mountain streams, a steep climb to Karatyurek. Glaciers and avalanches — only with experience. Ticks (encephalitis) in the forest belt. There is no mobile coverage — register your group with the Emergency Ministry.
food: Flatbreads and herbal tea at the Akkem weather station; dinners at the tourist bases in Tyungur (manty, home cooking); in Ust-Koksa — Smak café (4.9, 207 ratings, bill ~500 ₽), the vegetarian Ganga (4.9, 399 ratings, ~750 ₽); local honey and maral (Altai red deer) products from the Uimon valley
reviews: 2GIS: “Lake Akkem” 4.7 (10 ratings); Vysotnik tourist complex in Tyungur 4.9 (79 ratings) — people praise the staff, food and guides, and criticize the prices and extra charges (banya 2,500–3,500 ₽/h). Typical pros of the route: the most spectacular view of Belukha, a good trail, infrastructure at the lake; cons: the long road to Tyungur, cold, crowds in July–August, expensive lifts.

p.sum: Lake Akkem is the base for admiring Belukha; 2 days on foot/by horse from Tyungur (≈40–42 km) or 3–4 days on a loop via Lake Kucherla and Karatyurek Pass. Logistics: bus/car to Tyungur (6.5–8 h from Gorno-Altaysk), a GAZ-66 to “Three Birches”, pack horses for your luggage, overnight stays in the Akkem hut or in a tent. Russian citizens need a passport (border zone); foreigners need an FSB permit in advance.

p.permits: Russian citizens: passport (border zone of the Katanda and other settlements of the Ust-Koksa district), check-in with the border guards at the lake; for the 5-km strip along the border a permit is needed. Foreigners: a permit from the FSB Border Directorate for the Altai Republic (Gorno-Altaysk, 94 Kommunistichesky Ave., +7 388-22 4-82-00; border commandant's office in Ust-Koksa +7 38848 20-000), apply 30 days ahead. Online group registration with the Emergency Ministry. A separate Belukha Park ticket is not required (2024); the 300 ₽ rate for regional protected areas from 07.2026 — to be clarified.
p.access: Not for older people without training or for small children on foot; children 8+ on horses with a guide — possible. Dogs — according to park rules, in the border zone — not found. The alternative is a helicopter.
